text:
alex_g: Hey infra team — onboarding a new customer project (icg-eu) in europe-north1. We're designing the VPC for two k8s clusters (prod + staging). Rough targets: ~200 nodes total, up to ~50 pods/node in peak burst (so ~10k pod IPs). Asking for advice on subnet sizing, Cloud NAT capacity, and which quotas we should request bumped with GCP. Also worried about static IP quotas for NAT and per-region address limits. Any standard formula or examples?

mira: @alex_g recommend using GKE with alias IPs + secondary ranges. For ~10k pods I'd pick a pod secondary range /18 (16k addresses) and a service range /22. Node subnet can be small (e.g., /23 or /22) since it's ~200 nodes. That keeps room for scaling and avoids overlapping.

jamie_ops: Two practical asks for quota ticket: 1) raise regional Static External IPs in europe-north1 (we often need multiple reserved IPs for Cloud NAT + ILBs during canary rollouts). 2) increase number of VPC subnet secondary ranges (some org policies limit secondary ranges per subnet). I'd request based on expected max clusters: e.g., static IPs -> 64, secondary ranges -> 50.

samir: A note on Cloud NAT scaling — NAT uses ephemeral ports; if we have lots of concurrent connections per pod you can hit port exhaustion. Best practice: spread egress across multiple NAT IPs and use multiple NAT gateways if needed. For 10k pods with moderate outbound concurrency assume ~10 ports/pod -> 100k ports; one IP gives ~64k ports, so plan for >=2 NAT IPs and prefer 8-16 to be safe depending on workload.

alex_g: Good call. What's the cost hit if we reserve, say, 16 static IPs for NAT vs 4? Need numbers for the justification.

cloud-billing-bot: Est. monthly delta for static reserved IPs in europe-north1: 4 static IPs -> ~$8/month (GCP charges small holding fee), 16 static IPs -> ~$32/month. Cloud NAT egress (assuming 50 TB/mo) -> ~$5,500/mo (egress + NAT processing). If we add 12 more static IPs to distribute ports, only the small static-ip holding fees change; main cost is egress. Breakdown: "Static IPs (16)": "$32/mo", "Estimated egress (50TB)": "$5,500/mo", "Total est incremental": "$5,532/mo".

mira: For the quota request we should also include the VPC route quota (some regions hit max routes when we create a lot of node pools with custom routes). Ask GCP for increases to: "Static Addresses (regional)", "Subnetworks (secondary IP ranges)", and "Routes per VPC". Include our projected growth matrix and the terraform plan output.

gcp-support: Quick checklist to put in the GCP quota/support request: 1) Project ID: <INSERT_PROJECT_ID>. 2) Region: europe-north1. 3) Quotas to increase and requested limits (e.g., Static Addresses (region) -> 64; Subnetwork secondary IP ranges per VPC -> 50; Routes per VPC -> 10000). 4) Usage justification: expected nodes, pods, peak connections, and retention of reserved IPs for NAT and ILBs. 5) Attach network diagram + terraform snippet for subnet + sample pod IP calculations. Use this form: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/quota and paste the numbers in the body.

gcp-support: Example support ticket body (copy-paste friendly):
```
Subject: quota increase request for project PROJECT_ID in europe-north1
We request increases for the following quotas to support two GKE clusters (prod/staging) with up to 200 nodes and ~10k pods total:
- Static Addresses (regional, europe-north1): increase to 64
- Subnetwork secondary IP ranges per VPC: increase to 50
- Routes per VPC: increase to 10000
Justification: We will use alias IPs and secondary ranges to allocate ~16k pod IPs (/18) and /22 for services. We will reserve multiple static IPs for Cloud NAT to avoid port exhaustion and for internal load balancing during rollout. Expected egress ~50 TB/mo. Attach: network_diagram.png, terraform_plan.txt
```

alex_g: Perfect, thanks. I'll prepare the ticket. Attaching the terraform snippet we'll use for the pod secondary range and Cloud NAT config:```resource "google_compute_subnetwork" "k8s" {
  name = "k8s-subnet"
  ip_cidr_range = "10.100.0.0/22" # nodes
  secondary_ip_range {
    range_name    = "pods"
    ip_cidr_range = "10.200.0.0/18"
  }
  secondary_ip_range {
    range_name    = "services"
    ip_cidr_range = "10.210.0.0/22"
  }
  region = "europe-north1"
}

resource "google_compute_router" "nat-router" {
  name    = "nat-router"
  network = google_compute_network.vpc.name
  region  = "europe-north1"
}

resource "google_compute_router_nat" "nat" {
  name                               = "cloud-nat"
  router                             = google_compute_router.nat-router.name
  region                             = "europe-north1"
  nat_ip_allocate_option             = "MANUAL_ONLY"
  nat_ips                            = [google_compute_address.nat-ip.*.self_link]
  min_ports_per_vm                   = 64
  source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat = "ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES"
}
```

jamie_ops: LGTM. When you open the support ticket, add a short line about our mitigation plan if they need to approve incrementally (we can start with 16 IPs + /18 pod range and scale further). Also request expedited review because this customer has an SLA kickoff next month.

alex_g: Will do. I'll post the ticket link here once created and ping @mira for the network diagram review. Thanks all :thumbsup:
